purpose: Chenodiol is used to dissolve certain types of gallstones — specifically small cholesterol gallstones — in people who cannot or do not want to have surgery. It works best for people who have gallstones that are not too large and have a functioning gallbladder. It is taken by mouth over a long period of time, sometimes months to years.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes a substance called bile, which helps digest fats. Chenodiol is a natural bile acid that works by reducing the amount of cholesterol your body puts into bile, making the bile less likely to form stones. Over time, this allows existing cholesterol gallstones to slowly dissolve. Think of it like gradually dissolving a sugar cube in water — it takes time but the stone slowly breaks down.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is diarrhea, which can happen in many patients, especially at the start of treatment. You may also notice mild stomach upset, nausea, or cramping. Your liver enzymes may also increase, which is why your doctor will check your blood regularly while you take this medicine.
warnings: This medication can affect your liver, so regular blood tests are very important while you are taking it. It should NOT be used during pregnancy because it can harm an unborn baby — use reliable birth control while taking this medicine. Tell your doctor right away if you have yellowing of your skin or eyes, severe stomach pain, or unusual fatigue. People with certain liver diseases or bile duct problems should not use this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is about 13 to 16 mg per kilogram of your body weight per day, divided into two doses — one in the morning and one at night, taken with food or milk to reduce stomach upset. Your doctor will calculate the right dose for your specific weight. Treatment can last many months, and your doctor will monitor your progress with ultrasounds and blood tests along the way.
